standard_prerequisites.name: The S-module structure induced by a ring map R to S
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 725-726
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets an R-generating set be read as an S-generating set, since scalars from R act through their images in S.

core_obligations: Observe that every R-generating set of M is also an S-generating set, because the R-module structure on M is the one obtained by restriction of scalars along R to S (proof lines 725-726).
Conclude that finiteness of M as an R-module implies finiteness as an S-module (statement line 721).
proof_roadmap: Take a finite R-generating set and show it generates M over S as well, using that the two module structures agree on the image of R (proof lines 724-727).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for a ring map R to S and an S-module M, finiteness of M over R forces finiteness over S (statement lines 717-722). The proof does not construct a smaller generating set or use finite generation of S over R: it observes that an R-generating set is automatically S-generating, because the R-structure on M is induced by the image of R in S and so the S-scalar action covers the R-scalar action on that set (proof lines 724-727). This is the restriction-of-scalars bookkeeping that the statement's two module structures hide, and the author writes it out in one sentence. H2.
